result:
All three solutions give $\binom{N+1}{3}=\frac{(N-1)N(N+1)}{6}$, so they agree on the answer.

The count is right: the number of multisets of size 3 from $\{2,\dots,N\}$ is $\binom{N+1}{3}$. The key claim is that distinct sorted triples give non-isomorphic surfaces. Solution 1 asserts this with only a sketch. Solution 2 openly flags its topological argument as incomplete. Solution 3 relies on log Kodaira dimension and log canonical models, which is plausible but also only sketched. I could not verify the non-isomorphism claim independently, so my confidence is moderate. Solution 1 is the cleanest presentation of the same answer.

CHOICE: 1
